chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Garland's pianist, bassists and guitarists
summary: Freddie Gibbs played piano, Elbert Reynolds and John Williams bass, and various unnamed guitarists, as players came and went with gigs.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Freddie Gibbs was the piano player. Freddie Gibbs. He lived out in Long Island. Sometimes he had a group of his own.
And then did you have a bass player, too?
Yes. Elbert Reynolds started with.... Yeah, Elbert was working with Joe for years, a long time. And then after that, he used John Williams sometimes. He used different bass players.
Towards the end he started using a guitar, too; different guitar players. He had three or four different guitar players. I don't know their names. But Joe used

very good guitar players. The last one was a fellow named Charlie, but I never did know his last name. And I am not the most sociable type of person. I don't walk up to people and ask them, "What's your name?" But he was all right. A gig is a gig, you know. You figured, well, this is just this night(?), one of them things.
You'd never know who you were working with, because he didn't keep no set group of men. You couldn't keep them, because they'd get whatever comes up. They'd take what's out there for them.
